title: Document catalog
description: Which documents a venture makes, in which format, from which records, and in what order (EE-218), at packages/naive/src/functions/documents.json. A record is the source of truth and a document is an artifact rendered from records, never the record. The catalog is opinionated: each format says what it is for and the rules say when slides beat a printed document, so an agent does not guess. The ladder is the order every document climbs, a printable reading copy a person approved before any interactive page and the page before the live site; each rung names the extra records and decision classes it needs, in the shape packages/naive/src/engine/prerequisites.ts reads (EE-217). packages/naive/src/checks/check-documents.ts checks what this schema cannot: one root rung, no cycle, every kind's rungs reachable, every format and function known, every section's record path in the data model, and a venture's own document artifacts climbing in order.

formats.description: The formats a document may be rendered in. A format is a way of reading, not a tool: the tool that writes it is the renderer.

rung.description: The ladder rung this format sits on.

reads.description: How a person takes it in: alone and in order, on a screen, or in a room with a speaker.

prints.description: True when a person can print it and carry it into a meeting.

renderer.description: naive: naive render writes it in house, so the framework carries no heavy dependency. harness: the agent's own harness writes it from the reading copy, and the harness adapter (packages/naive/src/interfaces/adapters/) names the skill, so the catalog names no vendor. site-build: the venture's site build and the publishing gate (EE-025).

why.description: Why this format exists in the catalog, in one plain sentence.

rules.description: The opinionated part: how to choose a format. Each rule asks one question about the reader and names the format it points to. A rule never decides alone; a person may override it, and the override is a decision.

when.description: The reader's situation, in one plain sentence.

ladder.description: The order a document climbs. Fail closed: a rung is built only once the rung it comes after exists as a live artifact a person approved.

after.description: The rung below this one, or null for the first rung. Exactly one rung has null.

approved_by.description: Only a person approves a rung. An agent drafts and renders.

requires.description: What this rung needs beyond the rung below it, in the shape packages/naive/src/engine/prerequisites.ts reads (EE-217). The rung below is the ladder's own requirement and is not repeated here.

records.description: Logical record paths or route patterns that must be live.

meetings.description: Meeting kinds that must have happened.

decisions.description: Decision classes that must be decided by a person.

kinds.description: The documents this framework is opinionated about. A kind a venture wants and the catalog lacks is a pull request, not a local invention.

function.description: The function in packages/naive/src/functions/departments.json whose agent drafts it.

purpose.description: What the reader can do once they have read it.

artifact_kind.description: The artifact kind the rendered document is, as artifact.schema.json names it.

highest_rung.description: The top rung this kind climbs to. Most kinds stop at the reading copy.

why_format.description: Why these formats and not the others, in one plain sentence.

approves.description: The role that approves it, when it is not the founder. A person either way.

words_per_page.description: An unvalidated prior: about how many words belong on one page or one slide of this kind. A venture overrides it in naive.config.json.

pages.description: An unvalidated prior: about how many pages or slides this kind runs to.

sections.description: The reading copy's sections, in order. Each names the record it reads, so every claim in the rendered document cites a record.

from.description: The logical path of the record it reads, such as foundation/problem.json. A path with * reads every record it matches, one block each.

field.description: A dotted path to a string or a list of strings in that record. Without it the section names the record and leaves the words to the writer.

optional.description: True when a hole is left out instead of shown: a missing record, or a record with nothing in the field, leaves the section out rather than printing what is not recorded.
